title: Meta Tag Analyzer: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Meta Tag Analyzer](/meta-tag-analyzer) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Check a live page's title and description length and quality. Enter your page URL and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Check the meta tags that already exist on a live page: the title tag and meta description, their lengths, and whether they are missing, too short or too long — plus the canonical tag, robots meta and Open Graph tags for context. This tool CHECKS existing tags; the Meta Tag Generator on this site CREATES new ones for a page you are building. The fetch runs from this site's server with the usual safety limits, and nothing is stored.

## How to use the Meta Tag Analyzer

Start by typing or pasting your page URL. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste the full URL of the page to analyse, starting with https://.
2. Run the analysis and read the title and description lengths.
3. Rewrite anything flagged as missing, short or long.

## How it works

The [Meta Tag Analyzer](/meta-tag-analyzer) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Analyzing a page with a 42-character title and a 148-character description reports both as a good length, with the canonical tag and Open Graph tags listed for context. Try the same figures in the [Meta Tag Analyzer](/meta-tag-analyzer) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Meta Tag Analyzer](/meta-tag-analyzer) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## Lengths that work

Titles work best at roughly 50–60 characters — longer ones get cut off in search results — and descriptions at 120–160 characters. Shorter is not automatically bad: a clear 45-character title beats a padded 60-character one. The analyzer flags anything outside the usual ranges so you can judge it, and it flags missing tags as failures, because a page with no title or description is leaving its search snippet to chance.

## Analyzer vs. generator

This tool reads the tags a live page already has. The Meta Tag Generator does the opposite: it writes new tags for a page you are building, from a form. Use the generator when creating a page, and this analyzer when checking one that is already live.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Titles: roughly 50–60 characters. Descriptions: 120–160.
- A missing title or description is a failure — fix it first.
- Write for people, not for the character count.

## Frequently asked questions

### What does a meta tag analyzer do?

It fetches a live page and checks its title tag and meta description — whether they exist, how long they are, and whether they are in the range that displays well in search results. Try it with your own numbers in the [Meta Tag Analyzer](/meta-tag-analyzer) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How long should a title tag be?

Roughly 50–60 characters. Longer titles get cut off in search results; much shorter ones waste the space. Try it with your own numbers in the [Meta Tag Analyzer](/meta-tag-analyzer) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How long should a meta description be?

Roughly 120–160 characters. Longer descriptions get cut off, and a missing one leaves the snippet to the search engine. Try it with your own numbers in the [Meta Tag Analyzer](/meta-tag-analyzer) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is the difference from the Meta Tag Generator?

The analyzer checks tags that already exist on a live page. The generator creates new tags for a page you are building. Try it with your own numbers in the [Meta Tag Analyzer](/meta-tag-analyzer) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
